Details

Sample: every M3 recipe track (χ² < 1, 4 clusters, one ray per event) crossing det3’s interior, golden row sat_det3 (mx17_det3_saturday_scan_6-27-26 / long_run_resist_490V_drift_1000V), production table …/mx17_3/wft/final_phys/events.parquet (phys bundle, PIVOT_START). "Recoverable" counts only what a reference-free change was shown to recover on these very events (re-running the production reconstruction with the change, then scoring against M3): competing-cluster cut 2.1; spark veto (with the cut relaxed) 0.3; 2-strip seeds 0.26. The MULTI share (the M3 particle is among the candidates but another one was chosen) and the saturated-blob share are discussed on their slides and are NOT in this number.

Reproduce: rerun/satstudy/: satfit.py extract/fit, examples.py, sparks.py, railstats.py, reco_variant.py (three runs), summarize.py, make_deck.py. Outputs in ~/x17/cosmic_bench/satstudy/.

M3 reference

4

Details

Split of all 126 interior rays in the spark category (sparks.py), from the full-plane waveforms: discharge = a view with > 150 strips above SNR 6 or > 100 strips swinging below −10 σ (chip-wide ringing); muon+other = in both views the charge on the M3 footprint is a single, track-wide cluster and anything else sits > 5 mm away; shower = the rest (the cluster at the crossing is wide or branching). Checked by eye on random displays of each class.

What a discharge looks like here: the strips of whole DREAM chips (64 channels) jump together in the same samples — horizontal bands in the display — with saturated strips and a negative swing on hundreds of channels. In most examples the muon’s own trace is visible on M3 before the band, consistent with the earlier finding that det3 sparks are muon-induced (4× more likely with a track).

“muon+other” is mostly a clean track plus either a second particle far away or a slow baseline swing on a distant chip that crosses the 10 % floor (the floor is relative to the brightest strip, and a modest MIP makes it low). The 50-hit veto counts both planes together, so an inclined track (40+ strips in y) plus anything else trips it.

Recovery test: the production reconstruction (reco_variant.py --no-spark-veto, finalize environment) on all 126, scored with the budget’s rule (both views, r ≤ 5 mm, n_dropped ≤ 2). discharge: 2/32 detected as production would count it (r ≤ 5 mm AND n_dropped ≤ 2), 5 within 5 mm, chosen fit agreeing with M3 in both views in 4, some candidate agreeing in both views in 4; muon+other: 0/49 detected as production would count it (r ≤ 5 mm AND n_dropped ≤ 2), 20 within 5 mm, chosen fit agreeing with M3 in both views in 19, some candidate agreeing in both views in 34; shower: 4/45 detected as production would count it (r ≤ 5 mm AND n_dropped ≤ 2), 4 within 5 mm, chosen fit agreeing with M3 in both views in 0, some candidate agreeing in both views in 0. The chosen fits that agree carry n_dropped = 24–86 (muon+other): the other deposit is a competing cluster, so with the veto gone they would still fall to the n_dropped > 2 cut. Lifting the veto recovers them only together with the cut decision of the “found, cut” category; and like MULTI, 15 of the 49 have M3 only among the runners-up.

A better rule than a hit count: veto on the discharge signature itself (chip-wide simultaneous bands, the negative swing), and let the candidate fit handle busy-but-clean events.

5

Details

198 interior MULTI event-views where the chosen fit disagrees with M3 (|dθ| > 5° or |res| > 3 mm). In 64 % of them one of the other candidates (the seeder offers up to 3 clusters per plane) agrees with M3. So yes: two good tracks were reconstructed and production took the other. In the remaining 36 % the M3 particle’s cluster was not among the top 3, or merged with the other deposit.

The other particle is a separate track a median 72 mm away (10–90 %: 27–156 mm), in time with the muon (t0 difference median -15 ns, inside ±120 ns for 80 %), and brighter (median charge ratio 1.7×), which is why the largest-cluster ranking prefers it. A random second cosmic in the 1.9 µs window is ~10⁻⁴; these are correlated: shower companions or secondaries from the material above.

Can a better algorithm recover them? Not without the reference, and that is the point: both tracks are real, and a reference-free rule cannot know which one M3 followed. Measured on C22’s outliers (twotrack.py, % of MULTI views agreeing with M3): production 22 %, largest charge 22 %, lowest χ²/dof 50 %, t0 closest to the other view 38 %, any candidate (the ceiling) 67 %. For physics the multi-track output keeps both; for an efficiency the test-beam convention (any candidate within a wide window, nearest.py) counts these as detected. Neither changes the detector.

δ-rays: a knock-on electron leaves its own track; the straight-line fit takes both

Rutherford knock-on rate vs what det3 shows · event 28537

DELTA class

controls

M3 reference

production fit

6

Details

Physically: the muon kicks an atomic electron hard. The rate of a knock-on above T falls as ξ/T (ξ ≈ 0.34 keV for 30 mm of argon at 1 atm), and its path length rises steeply with T: a 10 keV δ goes ~2 mm (a blob), a 30 keV one ~1 cm, a 50 keV one ~3 cm (CSDA path in argon, approximate: ESTAR water values scaled by the stopping-power ratio; the projected extent is shorter because the electron scatters). So about 1 % of crossings carry a δ long enough to widen the cluster by ≳ 8 mm — the classifier’s threshold — and the observed DELTA share is 0.93 %.

In the data: a wide cluster that grows sideways out of the track at one depth, often curling, often ending in a bright spot (where the electron stops and dE/dx peaks). The fit has one straight line and a non-negative charge profile along it, so it tilts to pass through the δ’s charge.

Recoverable? Partly, in principle: the muon’s part of the column is usually still straight and on M3. The two-track fit does not do it (it looks for a second straight line: any candidate agrees in 10 % of DELTA views with it on, vs 8 % in production). A robust fit that down-weights charge far from the line, or a track + free-form-blob model, could. Not tried here. The gas mixture of the June bench was not recorded; ξ uses pure argon, which the few-% quencher changes by a few %.

7

Details

Code: wft/model.py. prep_plane builds the mask sat = W_raw ≥ SAT (SAT = the bundle’s sat_adc = 3550, on the pedestal + CM subtracted samples before the gain division; dead channels are added to the same mask). _solve_nnls drops masked samples from the weighted NNLS for the depth-charge profile, then adds Σ max(0, W − model)² / σ² over the masked samples: the model is pushed up to the clip but never pulled down. The χ² dof count excludes them. WFT_SAT_SOLVE=1 (opt-in, off in production) re-solves with the model held at the clip on samples where it falls below (a Tobit active set); FINDINGS §41 found it does not fix the 5–12 % charge deficit of saturated tracks, and that angle/position were unchanged by censoring on the bench resolution sample.

Nothing else knows about saturation: the rest of a clipped strip’s samples — the rising edge, the falling edge after the plateau and the undershoot — are fitted with the same linear, amplitude-independent electronics template as an unsaturated strip, and so are the neighbours’ copies through the sharing kernel. Next slide: what the rail actually looks like.

The rail is not at 3550, and the more strips sit on it, the more fits fail

det3 waveforms (1,324 events) · all golden-row fits, one-cluster views

x view

y view

8

Details

Left: the maximum of every strip above 3000 ADC in the satfit sample. The pile-up is the ADC rail, 4095 − pedestal − common mode: it sits at 3650–3900 and varies per channel and per sample, not at the bundle’s 3550. Within one clipped plateau the CM moves the clipped value by a median 72 ADC (90 %: 248); 1,729 of 44,697 samples inside a plateau (3.9 %) fall below 3550 and are fitted as exact measurements. Plateaus last a median 6 samples (360 ns).

The bottom rail. After the plateau, 58 % of clipped strips swing down to ADC 0: the strip’s max − min is 4100 ADC, the full 12-bit range (median undershoot -248 ADC; unsaturated bright strips undershoot by a median 2.1 % of their peak). Those bottom-clipped samples are fitted as data too. Whether the electronics are still linear there (a template undershoot of a 3–10× larger true pulse) or recovering from overload cannot be told from these strips alone.

Right: production fits, views with one hit cluster, by the number of saturated hits. Fraction disagreeing with M3 (|dθ| > 5° or |res| > 3 mm). 10 % (x) and 11 % (y) of views have ≥ 3 saturated strips. When a saturated fit fails, it reads too STEEP in 90 % (x) / 86 % (y) of cases (median |tan| excess 0.32 / 0.64); χ²/dof median: failed 2336, saturated-but-fine 438, unsaturated 40 (x).

Saturation is correlated with everything else that is bright (δ-rays, blobs, two particles), so the right panel is not by itself the effect of the censoring rule: the next two slides separate them.

What a failed saturated track looks like: a faint MIP line plus one compact, very bright blob

the blob is a short δ-electron stopping: 5–20 keV in 1–5 mm, 1–3× the whole MIP track’s charge on 2–4 strips

M3 reference

production fit

sample ≥ 3550 (censored)

9

Details

Most FIT_SAT failures are not a saturated MIP column. The track itself is faint and on M3; the saturated strips belong to one compact deposit deep in the gap, often 1–4 mm off the line. A low-energy knock-on electron (δ) of 5–20 keV travels only 1–5 mm in argon, depositing as much charge as the whole MIP track (≈ 3 cm × ~2.5 keV/cm) on a few strips — so it saturates them. P(T > 5 keV) ≈ 7 %, P(T > 10 keV) ≈ 3 % per crossing (previous slide’s ξ/T), the same order as the 10 % of views with ≥ 3 saturated strips.

Why the fit fails: its model is one straight line with a non-negative charge profile along it. The blob holds most of the charge, so χ² is dominated by it and the line tilts to reach it (the "too steep" of the previous slide). The next slide tests whether the treatment of the clipped samples is to blame: it is not — even with every saturated strip removed the line still tilts, because the blob’s unsaturated edges and neighbours hold enough charge off the MIP line.

So the fix aimed at this failure is the model, not the mask: a straight track + one free compact deposit (position, time, charge, its own width), which would let the MIP part fix the line.

Changing the censoring moves saturated views by +2 points at most: the rail is not what misleads the fit

10

Details

satfit.py: each saturated event (≥ 3 saturated hits in a view; 924 events) and 400 unsaturated controls, refitted with the production fitter (wft.reco.fit_plane, phys bundle, t0 prior, WFT_PIVOT_START=1, which reproduces the table to < 0.05 mm) on a rebuilt window (the SNR > 6 cluster under the production fit ± 3 strips). Only the censor mask changes between arms: low = censor ≥ 3300; both = ≥ 3300 and, on a strip that clipped, every sample ≤ −200 dropped; tail = everything after a strip’s first clipped sample; strip = every sample of a clipped strip. Numbers above the bars: views that start / stop agreeing with M3 against production.

Controls have no saturated sample, so only low/both can change them (the 3300 cut can catch a bright unsaturated sample).

Reading it: the failures are 91 % angle and 74 % position failures in production, and their |dθ| 90th percentile stays at ~31° under every rule. The rules do lower χ²/dof (the clipped and bottom-rail samples were badly modelled), but the line does not move: the blob’s rising edges and its unsaturated neighbours (through the sharing kernel) carry enough charge off the MIP line to tilt it on their own. Any rule in the set agrees in 77 % of views (vs 71 %), so per-event rule shopping would not help either.

What this does not test: an amplitude-dependent template, a per-channel rail from the pedestal file, or a track + blob model. The first two are about charge (FINDINGS §41), not geometry; the third is the one aimed at this failure.

“Clean, fit off” is mostly two close tracks the classifier could not separate

FIT class, 0.34 % of interior rays: no saturation, one cluster within 5 mm of M3

two tracks a few mm apart, or a V from one point: the fit lands between them

M3 reference

production fit

11

Details

The C22 classifier calls a view "clean" when nothing else sits more than 5 mm from the footprint and the cluster is not too wide. By eye most FIT events are two tracks within a few mm (parallel, or a V from a common vertex: a δ emitted forward, or a pair), plus some long-tailed single tracks. A single straight line goes between them.

Recoverable? This is the two-track fit’s regime, below its separation limit (notes/two-track-limit: the trigger fires on ~0 % of inclined pairs under 12 mm). With WFT_TWO_TRACK_FIT=1 any candidate agrees in 35 % vs 34 % without: no gain today. Small share.

“Fit failed” is never a fit: a 2-strip x cluster never reaches the fitter

above the floor (seeds)

noise

17/17 have x charge on M3 at SNR 100–500 on 2 strips; the 3rd strip is at 7–9 % of the brightest

17 of 17 detected with MIN_STRIPS = 2

controls: 400/400 vs 400/400 detected, 0 views moved

12

Details

All 17 interior "fit failed" rays have the same signature: the y view is fitted and agrees with M3; the x view has no row at all in the candidate table and x_ftst = −1 (the plane was never windowed). The x hits are on the M3 footprint (2 strips at hundreds of σ), but a near-vertical x track in det3 shares little charge (the x kernel c1 = 0.05), so its ±1 neighbours sit at 7–9 % of the brightest strip — 30σ signals, but under the 10 % relative floor, which leaves 2 strips, one short of MIN_STRIPS = 3. Over the whole golden row, 34 x planes and 7 y planes end up with < 3 strips after the floor.

Recoverable: yes. Re-running the production reconstruction with MIN_STRIPS = 2 (reco_variant.py --min-strips 2): 17 of 17 detected with MIN_STRIPS = 2. controls: 400/400 vs 400/400 detected, 0 views moved. Alternatives that keep MIN_STRIPS: an absolute SNR floor next to the relative one (a strip at 30σ is not noise), or the local floor already in the beam seeder.

The rest is either a cut we chose or the reference’s own error

the remaining det3 interior categories

Found, cut: 2.1 %

The fit is on M3, but another cluster in the view has > 2 strips (n_dropped). Recoverable by choosing the cut: decision 2 of the C22 handoff.

Position tail: 0.22 %

Right angle, one clean cluster, > 3 mm from M3. About ⅔ are muons that scattered between the M3 doublets (a kink a 4-layer χ² < 1 cannot see). The reference is wrong; nothing to recover.

Edge: 0.29 %

Interior by the budget’s rule but near the edge of the OTHER coordinate (< 8 mm) or the field distortion zone: a truncated or bent column. Geometry, not reconstruction.

13

Details

C22 report (notes/mx17-outliers-vs-m3) has the evidence for the bent-track fraction (kinkvtx.py: 0.65 ± 0.07 of the position tail) and the edge response.
